Start the server with **`--root-path /api`** so FastAPI knows the prefix your proxy adds.

**Why the docs break:** When you open the integrated docs UI (the frontend), it would expect to get the OpenAPI schema at `/openapi.json`, instead of `/api/v1/openapi.json`.[1] In your case, it needs to fetch `/api/openapi.json`.

**Fix:**

```console
$ fastapi run main.py --forwarded-allow-ips="*" --root-path /api
```

FastAPI uses this `root_path` to create the default `server` in OpenAPI with the URL provided by `root_path`.[3] Then open the docs through the proxy, at `/api/docs`. If you try the docs UI served by the server directly, without the path prefix in the URL, it won't work, because it expects to be accessed through the proxy.[3]

**Notes:**

- This setup assumes Nginx strips the prefix before forwarding, so your app still sees routes like `/app`. The proxy would be "stripping" the path prefix on the fly before transmitting the request to the server, keeping your application convinced that it is being served at `/app`[1]. The docs' example uses Traefik, but the same `root_path` setting applies. The excerpts I have don't cover the Nginx configuration itself.
- Don't set it in code. In FastAPI 0.145.0 and earlier, `root_path` could also be configured in `FastAPI()`. This parameter is now deprecated because its behavior was not consistent with the server configuration. Use `fastapi run --root-path /api/v1` instead.[4]
- To check that it worked, read `request.scope.get("root_path")` in an endpoint. It should return `"/api"`.
